p: There's an art to escape rooms, and it doesn't involve being clever so much as being organised. Search first, solve second. Gather your finds in one place, look for patterns between them, and keep checking in with each other about what you've tried. If a lock won't budge after a few honest attempts, step away and come back to it. Often the missing piece is hiding in the bit of the room you haven't properly searched yet.

It's also worth booking a room that matches your group's vibe. Fancy something spooky, something adventurous or something more light-hearted? Have a look at the themes on offer and choose together. A group that's excited about the story usually plays better. Turning up ten minutes early also means nobody misses the briefing, which often holds a useful hint or two about how the room works.

Kingston itself has some fun bits to discover once you're out. Just round the corner from Eden Walk, you'll find Out of Order, the much-photographed sculpture of toppled red phone boxes leaning like dominoes, which is a great spot for a group photo after your game. The Bentall Centre is right nearby for more shopping and food, and the Rose Theatre near the river puts on everything from drama to family shows. History fans should seek out the Coronation Stone outside the Guildhall, linked to the crowning of Saxon kings. For a bigger day out, Hampton Court Palace is a short hop away along the river, and the wide-open spaces and deer of Richmond Park are just to the north, perfect for walking off a post-game lunch.
